studies.Population: Adult men in the EPIC cohort
studies.Reference: Protein and amino acid intakes in relation to prostate cancer risk and mortality-A prospective study in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition.
studies.Authors: Schmidt JA, Huybrechts I, Overvad K, Eriksen AK, Tjønneland A, Kaaks R, Katzke V, Schulze MB, Pala V, Sacerdote C, Tumino R, Bueno-de-Mesquita B, Sánchez MJ, Huerta JM, Barricarte A, Amiano P, Agudo A, Bjartell A, Stocks T, Thysell E, Wennberg M, Weiderpass E, Travis RC, Key TJ, Perez-Cornago A
studies.Timing: Baseline dietary assessment with mean 16.2-year follow-up for prostate cancer mortality
studies.comparison_type: Highest fifth versus lowest fifth of egg-protein intake
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: protein and amino acid intakes were estimated using validated dietary questionnaires

sample_size.excerpt: In 131,425 men from the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition, protein and amino acid intakes were estimated using validated dietary questionnaires.

cases.excerpt: During a mean follow-up of 14.2 years, 6939 men were diagnosed with prostate cancer and 914 died of the disease.

effect_size.excerpt: For prostate cancer death, we observed no strong associations with protein or amino acid intakes, but the results suggested that men who consumed more protein from eggs might be at a higher risk of dying from prostate cancer (Figure 2 and Table S4 ). The HRs (95% CIs) in the second to the top fifths compared to the lowest fifth were 1.09 (0.87, 1.36), 1.13 (0.90, 1.42), 1.07 (0.86, 1.34) and 1.22 (0.98, 1.53; p trend = 0.1), respectively.
effect_size.location: Results, Risk of total prostate cancer and prostate cancer death

confidence_interval.excerpt: The HRs (95% CIs) in the second to the top fifths compared to the lowest fifth were 1.09 (0.87, 1.36), 1.13 (0.90, 1.42), 1.07 (0.86, 1.34) and 1.22 (0.98, 1.53; p trend = 0.1), respectively.
confidence_interval.location: Results, Risk of total prostate cancer and prostate cancer death

p_value.excerpt: The HRs (95% CIs) in the second to the top fifths compared to the lowest fifth were 1.09 (0.87, 1.36), 1.13 (0.90, 1.42), 1.07 (0.86, 1.34) and 1.22 (0.98, 1.53; p trend = 0.1), respectively.
p_value.location: Results, Risk of total prostate cancer and prostate cancer death

comparison.location: Results, Risk of total prostate cancer and prostate cancer death

design.excerpt: To prospectively investigate the associations of dietary intakes of total protein, protein from different dietary sources, and amino acids with prostate cancer risk and mortality.

timing.excerpt: During a mean follow-up of 14.2 years
